extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editorial staff of Clinical and Translational Gastroenterology (and other biomedical journal stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy for transitioning a biomedical journal from single-blind to double-blind peer review, including anonymization practices, procedural changes for submission, known limitations, and monitoring expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of double-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: With double-blind reviewing, neither the authors' nor reviewers' identities are shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with single-blind (where reviewers are anonymous but authors are known). Sets baseline expectation for what the review process will withhold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript anonymization / author instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will be instructed to avoid first person self-referencing and allusions to affiliations as much as possible; title pages with author and institutional information will be uploaded as an individual document, separate from the remainder of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procedural measures to facilitate blinding: remove identifying allusions and self-citations; separate title page upload. These steps facilitate blinding of manuscripts sent for external expert review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected blinding success and ways to improve it
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful blinding of author identity is achieved approximately 60% of the time and may be increased to 75% with the removal of identifying allusions and self-citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use evidence-based anonymization steps (e.g., remove self-citations/allusions) to improve the probability that reviewers cannot infer author identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of limits / unavoidable exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: Unintentional exposure of author or institution identity is sometimes unavoidable, such as in small, specialized fields or subsequent to early sharing of data at conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize double-blind is imperfect; accept that in some contexts identity will be inferable despite anonymization, and plan accordingly (e.g., transparency about limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale: mitigation of conscious and unconscious biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-blind reviews are intended to limit biases based on investigators' reputations, institutional prestige, race, and/or sex—whether conscious or not—bringing closer to an accurate assessment of the science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy motivated by documented associations between author/institution prestige and manuscript acceptance; use double-blind to reduce such influences on editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence that double-blind can improve review quality and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and surveys cited show that double-blind review was considered the most effective form of peer review (study of 40,000 authors) and that evidence suggests double-blind reviews are of higher quality than single-blind reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cited literature (meta-analyses, randomized trials, large surveys) to justify the change and to inform expectations about outcomes (quality and acceptance bias).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community consultation and buy-in as part of policy change
rubrics_metrics.description: CTG queried its community: with 88% author and 80% reviewer response rates, nearly 65% of respondents supported double-blind reviews; fewer than 10% disfavored it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather and report author/reviewer feedback and response rates to justify adopting the policy and to inform rollout decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational / staffing expectations and burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing double-blind review may impose an additional burden on both authors and CTG staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge resource/time costs upfront; weigh them against anticipated benefits when deciding to implement; prepare staff workflows to handle separate title-page uploads and anonymization checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, transparency, and iterative improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal will be self-monitoring the success of its efforts and welcoming feedback from authors, reviewers, and readers, addressing challenges in a transparent fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up monitoring metrics (e.g., blinding success rate, acceptance disparities) and feedback channels; use results to iteratively improve anonymization guidance and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of opposing arguments / trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments against double-blind review claim that successful blinding is cumbersome and it precludes comprehensive assessment of a manuscript and its authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh these trade-offs explicitly; document concerns and plan how to mitigate lost contextual information while preserving fairness.
